subject: Is my dataset not compatible with unmarked?

messages.author: d61cb3841e6d1820
messages.subject: Is my dataset not compatible with unmarked?
parts:
Dear all, 

I am having an infinite series of issue trying to use unmarked for analyzing my data. 
I hope that I can receive your help. 

I surveyed 10 sites for the presence of an animal, 5 of these sites were surveyed 18 times while the remaining 5 sites were surveyed 17 times. 
For each site and day, I sampled 20 different spots (i.e., by inspecting the ground). 

I melted the data corresponding to the same date and site with 
melt(dataset, , id.vars = c("id_site", "date", "sampling spot"))
in order to have a summary of the presence absence (binary 0-1) of my target for a certain date and site.
I obtained the attached dataframe consisting of 200 rows. 

However, my siteCovs have just 10 rows, corresponding to the characteristics of the 10 sampled sites. 
Also the obsCovs do not match with the structure required by unmarked, since it represent the characteristics of each sampling spot per date per site. 
I know that it is difficult to evaluate my case without seeing my dataset but I am wondering if the structure of my data are not compatible with this pakage. 

Obviously I tried to simplify and to run the models, and it worked. 
For instance, I melted again the y dataframe, obtaining 10 rows as the siteCovs dataframe. 
However, I wonder if this melting and melting makes my analysis poorer than if I would have used the 200 rows dataframe. 
In fact, the resulting occupancy models are quite depressing. 

Every suggestion is more than welcome, 
thank you for your kind attention. 

Sabina

messages.author: 0c8e4d9395a2aae5
messages.subject: Re: Is my dataset not compatible with unmarked?
parts:
Sabina, 

If you have 10 sites and 17 visits, then your site covariates would have 10 rows and your count data would have 17 columns and 10 rows.  Your observation data would have 17 * 10 rows.  The obs data corresponds to the repeat surveys and tends to include variables like observer, date, weather, etc.  Sounds like you're trying to use your data for the 200 sample locations as observation data?  If so, no, that shouldn't work.

One option for you is to use the 200 sample locations as your samples, so that your site covariates would have 200 rows.  You could then include 'site' as a covariate in your models, to account for differences among the 10 sites.  This would add 9 more coefficients to your model, which could be an issue given the amount of data you have, I'm not sure.  This would account for spatial correlation among the 20 samples at a site.  But if your objective is to learn specifics about different variables at your 10 sites, this method wouldn't tell you much. 

This hierarchical arrangement of samples within sites is perfect for mixed models, but as I understand unmarked does not include mixed models yet.  But apparently it could be done with a Bayesian approach that I have no experience with. 

Mike Worland
